sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s master how to pass 2D arrays to methods like a pro! You’ll learn:

• How to declare method parameters for 2D arrays
• The difference between passing arrays vs. single values
• Practical examples to use right away

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine a 2D array like a spreadsheet - rows and columns full of data. When you pass this spreadsheet to a method, you’re giving it the whole grid to work with!

**How it works:**
• A 2D array is just an array of arrays
• Methods can accept them as parameters
• The method can then read or modify the entire grid

**Key syntax:**
• Method declaration: `void processArray(int[][] arr)`
• Call the method: `processArray(my2DArray)`

The method gets access to all elements - no need to pass each value separately!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Pass a 2D array to a method with the parameter type dataType[][]
The method receives a reference to the original 2D array and can modify its elements
No need to specify row size in the parameter: public static void print(int[][] m)
Returning a 2D array from a method follows the same pattern as 1D arrays
Helper methods for 2D arrays improve code modularity and reusability

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Passing 2D arrays to methods is just like passing 1D arrays - use `[][]` syntax. Methods can read and modify the original array since it's passed by reference. Practice with real examples like matrix operations or game boards.

questions.question: What is the correct way to pass a 2D array to a method?
options: All of the above are valid
questions.explanation: Java allows multiple syntaxes for 2D array parameters: int[][] arr, int arr[][], and int[] arr[] are all valid ways to declare a 2D array parameter.

questions.question: When a 2D array is passed to a method, can the method modify the original array?
options: No, a copy is always made
Yes, because the reference is passed
Only the first row can be modified
Only if the method is static
questions.explanation: Like 1D arrays, 2D arrays are passed by reference. The method receives a reference to the original array, so modifications affect the original.
